newsitem.title: USA: Brazil coffee belt sees cool temps, no damage - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee belt sees cool temps, no damage - WSC.

text.p: Temperatures will cool to below normal levels in Brazil's coffee belt, but no damaging cold is expected, Weather Services Corp said in an update issued Wednesday.

This morning's skies were mostly fair, with temperatures near normal levels and lows ranging from 48 to 61 F (9 to 16 C). Scattered thunderstorms packing one to two inches of rain were reported in Northern Parana.

Fair to partly cloudy skies are expected for Thursday and Friday. Temperature lows will be in the 40s to low 50s F (5 to 12 C) by Friday morning. Fair to partly cloudy skies again on Saturday with temperatures staying mostly below normal, according to WSC.
Developing low pressure off the coast of Brazil during the next 24 hours will bring cooler air into the area.

"The airmass is building along the southeast coast of Argentina and is not expected to be cold enough to cause any damage in the coffee belt despite the favorable delivery pattern of cooler weather," WSC said. ((New York Commodity Desk, 212 859-1640))
